title: Injection Molding & Die Casting
painPoint: Injection molding and die casting cells live on fast mold changes, yet hydraulic clamping systems cost 20 to 40 minutes of downtime per swap and leak oil onto hot platens. Magnetic clamping plates solve the cycle-time problem but introduce a magnet problem of their own. Platen temperatures of 80 to 150 C in production, plus 200 C heat soak during purging and shutdown, push standard N42 blocks into irreversible loss. Backplates also need 12 to 15 kgf/cm2 of holding force held flat across the whole mold, or melt flashes and parts distort. Repeated clamp cycles, coolant mist and ferrous debris bridging pole gaps finish the job: arrays drift, crack and lose grip within months.
youjiuSolution: YOUJIU builds NdFeB magnet arrays for magnetic mold clamping plates and quick-change templates used on injection molding machines, die casters and press brakes. We standardize on 42SH, 38UH and 35EH grades whose intrinsic coercivity holds rated clamp force through 150 C platens and short excursions past 180 C, verified by irreversible loss testing at operating temperature. Pole layouts are flux-simulated for 14 kgf/cm2 uniform force on 300 to 1600 mm templates. Epoxy-sealed, NiCuNi-coated blocks resist coolant mist and ferrous debris. Send your platen size, mold weight and cycle profile for a graded clamp design and quote.
advantages: 42SH, 38UH and 35EH grades sustain 12-15 kgf/cm2 clamp force at 150 C platen temperature.
Irreversible loss stays under 3 percent after 180 C soak and 10,000 clamp cycles.
